hero.role: Software Engineer, Frontend Developer, and Community Leader
hero.description: I am a Wayuu woman from San Juan del Cesar, La Guajira, Colombia. I build modern web experiences that are easy to use and open to more people. My work connects tech, inclusion, women leaders, and Indigenous communities.
hero.imageAlt: Rina Plata smiling, wearing a black blazer and a Wayuu necklace

about.lead: I believe technology is only good when everyone can use it.
about.photoCaption: Wearing my Wayuu manta: my identity is in my code too.
about.title: More than code
about.description: My story connects software, frontend work, community, and Wayuu identity.
about.imageAlt: Rina Plata in a red Wayuu manta, smiling, on an orange background
paragraphs: I am Rina Plata, a software engineer with experience in frontend work, web access, and community leadership. I see tech as a tool to open doors, tell stories, and build products that feel more human.

I enjoy building clear and useful interfaces. I work with Angular, React, TypeScript, access needs, and UX good practices so more people can use digital products. I also use AI in my projects to save time and improve the user experience, with care and respect for users.
I also lead and join communities. I speak about education, web access, women in tech, native identity, and social impact.

plain.title: Plain Language Summary
plain.description: Here is the short version of this site.
items: I am Rina Plata, a Wayuu woman from San Juan del Cesar, La Guajira, and a software engineer.
I build websites and apps that are easier for people to use.
I work with teams, communities, and women in tech.
I share talks about code, access, identity, and learning.
You can see my work, talks, projects, and ways to contact me below.

jsconfmx-gestures.title: Control the Web with Gestures, Voice, and Gaze Using JavaScript
jsconfmx-gestures.description: A JSConf MX (Guadalajara) talk about accessible web interfaces that don't depend on a mouse or keyboard. Live demos with MediaPipe, WebGazer.js, and the Web Speech API show how AI can make experiences more inclusive in real time.

codinglatam-inclusion.title: Inclusion Is Also Coded
codinglatam-inclusion.description: A CodingLatam DevCon Honduras talk about types of disability, including temporary and situational ones, and the WCAG guidelines. Live, it audits a Honduran website, navigates with a screen reader, and controls a page with only gaze, face, or a hand gesture using WebGazer.js and MediaPipe.

caribeconf-2026-inclusion.title: Technology as a Tool for Inclusion
caribeconf-2026-inclusion.description: A talk at the second edition of CaribeConf in Barranquilla about how web development and AI can build products for everyone: speech recognition, eye tracking, and AI to remove access barriers.
